solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In trouble, poor man tries to become fraudster with new identity

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so the letters of the following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A struggling poor man resorts to fraud, adopting a false identity to escape his circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' rearranges all twelve letters of POOR MAN TRIES; 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who poses as another person is a fraudster who has taken on a fresh identity.

clue.text: Dominant female who takes a fellow in!

explanation.surface: A domineering woman who seduces and swallows up men.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal and comic: one who eats a man, taking him in as food rather than deceiving him.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically a predatory woman who dominates her lovers; literally a creature that devours people.

clue.text: A head teacher's part

indicators.note: a part of the word teacher's supplies the run of letters needed

explanation.surface: A remark about a portion belonging to a head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' reads as a person in charge, but means 'per head', as in a price for each person.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging a sum a head means charging it to every individual person, one by one.

clue.text: Concerned with certain matter in dependable country

parts.note: solid means reliable or dependable
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: Something about a particular issue in a trustworthy nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Solid-state physics studies matter in its solid form, which is what the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes the branch of physics dealing with matter in its rigid crystalline phase.

clue.text: Go wandering around with aunt? That's sweet!

indicators.note: letters wandering around move from their places into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Going for a stroll with one's aunt is a lovely thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering around' is one indicator; 'with' and 'That's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This chewy confection of nuts, honey and sugar is a type of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Terribly hot drink one imbibed? It's radioactive!

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the letters of the next word are disordered

parts.note: taken as the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A drink served dreadfully hot and gulped down turns out to be dangerously radioactive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's radioactive!' defines a substance, so the definition is the whole phrase, not just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: This metallic element is naturally radioactive and is used as a nuclear fuel.

clue.text: Toe ma roughly bashed? Medical specialist may know all about it

definitions.text: Medical specialist may know all about it

indicators.note: something bashed is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A badly bruised toe — a doctor in the right field would understand it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'bashed' rearranges TOE MA ROUGHLY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the branch of medicine dealing with joint and muscle disorders, a specialist's field of knowledge.

clue.text: Plant I left had to be pulled up, bad in the middle

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means read from the bottom upwards, so the letters are reversed
the centre letter of the word bad is taken

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a plant that had to be uprooted because it had rotted in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be pulled up' reverses I, L and HAD to give DAHLI; 'in the middle' takes A from bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden plant with showy flowers grown from tubers.

clue.text: Desperate man grabbing weak woman

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold of, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A frantic man seizes hold of a frail woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a hugely strong cowboy in the long-running British children's comic The Dandy; 'grabbing' puts W inside DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, used as the crossword's generic example of a woman.

clue.text: Tissue in room you finally drop

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word you

parts.note: to lose something is to drop or let it go

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop dropping paper hankies around the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes U, the last letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose is the fibrous substance that makes up plant tissue and paper tissues.

clue.text: Plants showing flowers half the day, up to the time of stars

indicators.note: keeping half of the word means dropping its second three letters

parts.note: Friday is a day of the week, here the one cut down
till means up to, as in waiting till noon
Aries is the zodiac sign governing a period of the year in astrology

explanation.surface: Flowers that open for part of the day and stay out until the stars come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' cuts FRIDAY to FRI; Aries is one of the star signs, ruling late March to April; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bulbous plants of the lily family, such as the snake's head fritillary.

clue.text: First couple of elephants in highway charge again

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letters go within the highway word

parts.note: a road is a highway

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the word elephants are taken

explanation.surface: A pair of elephants on a road launch a second charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The elephant charge misleads: the definition is about loading a weapon again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload a gun is to put a fresh charge of ammunition in it.

clue.text: One arrangement is made initially — it's unrealistic

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a deal is an arrangement or agreement

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word made

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a single proposed agreement as impractical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes M from 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is pursuing perfect principles, often criticised as impractical or out of touch with reality.

clue.text: Excessively optimistic Tories tend to look silly

indicators.note: made to look silly means put into a ridiculous shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Conservative politicians often seem foolish when they are too hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to look silly' rearranges the ten letters of TORIES TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing through rose-coloured glasses is an idiom for an unrealistically cheerful outlook.

clue.text: Traffic lane

parts.note: reads as a lane on a motorway, but traffic here is commerce, so the lane is a path used for commerce between places

explanation.walkthrough: Traffic means trade, as in drug trafficking, rather than vehicles on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial path along which merchants carry goods is a lane for traffic in the trading sense.

clue.text: Pour out, making the enemy retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: time is called the old enemy, as in 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: Discharging something forces opposing troops to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the enemy' is a crossword convention for TIME; 'retreat' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, such as smoke or light.

clue.text: Like some steroids manufactured in a lab co.

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up out of raw material, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Certain steroids are produced in a laboratory company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges IN A LAB CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids promote muscle growth; anabolic describes that tissue-building type.

clue.text: Lechery of army officer outside America

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
US stands for the United States of America

explanation.surface: The lewd behaviour of a soldier serving abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lust is strong sexual desire, which is what lechery means.

clue.text: Element in soil (not oxygen) I study

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed from the word soil

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone studies a chemical element in the soil, excluding oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes O from SOIL to leave SIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicon is a chemical element, very common in the earth's crust.

clue.text: Anniversary organised in canteen, attended by fifty

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so these letters are arranged differently

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A birthday party is held in the canteen, with fifty guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges IN CANTEEN; 'attended by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A centennial is a hundredth anniversary, the anniversary marking a century.

clue.text: I 'cry a river' — it shows you the pressure!

parts.note: to sob is to cry
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone cries an ocean, saying it reveals how much stress they are under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cry a river' reads as a phrase meaning weep a lot, but splits into SOB, A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Song about sailor somewhere in the Middle East

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sea shanty about a sailor travelling to a place in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabia is the peninsula of southwest Asia, a region of the Middle East.

clue.text: Everyone sent to work unit? I start to cower, having an aversion

parts.note: all means everyone
the erg is a unit of work or energy in physics

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word cower

explanation.surface: When everyone is sent off to work, someone begins to cower because they hate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes C from 'cower'; 'sent to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allergic to something, figuratively, means having a strong dislike of it.

clue.text: Old boy has itch to be 'not square'

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy yearns to be trendy rather than conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not square' reads as slang for being cool, but means a rectangle with unequal sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is precisely a four-sided figure that is no square.

clue.text: Field engineers brought in by emergency organisation

indicators.note: brought in by means taken inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British breakdown recovery service
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers are called in by a breakdown service.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is a British motoring organisation that rescues broken-down cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or activity is an area of it.

clue.text: Hospital apparatus in country facing Tory cut

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean country

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word Tory loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Hospital equipment in a country faces cuts from the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of TORY to give TOR; 'facing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubator is a heated enclosure used in hospitals to nurse premature babies.

clue.text: Film director's meaty stuff

definitions.meaning: David ... directed Lawrence of Arabia and Brief Encounter
the meat without fat on it

explanation.surface: A film director's substantial work.
explanation.walkthrough: David Lean was a British director of epics such as Lawrence of Arabia; 'meaty' suggests weighty work but means actual meat.
explanation.definitionFit: David Lean is the film director; lean also means meat free of fat.

clue.text: Two features in a musical creating a fuss

definitions.meaning: singing and dancing are two elements of musical theatre
an idiom for an unnecessary commotion

explanation.surface: Two parts of a stage show cause a great commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally singing plus dancing in a show; idiomatically a needless commotion made over something.
